stem: A 13-year-old presents to the Emergency Department with a life-threatening condition and no parent can be contacted; what is the best next step?

options.text: Wait until a parent or guardian is reached before giving treatment
Proceed with emergency or life-saving treatment without the consent of the minor or parents
Treat only if two consultants independently agree
Do not treat unless the child is already assessed as Gillick competent

explanation: Emergency or life-saving treatment can proceed without consent from the minor or parents. In a life-threatening situation, treatment should not be delayed while waiting for consent or court approval.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Emergency treatment may be given without prior consent when immediate care is required to prevent serious harm or death.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because life-saving treatment should not be delayed until a parent or guardian can be contacted.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because emergency or life-saving treatment may be provided without consent when immediate treatment is required to prevent serious harm or death.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because there is no requirement for two consultants to agree before giving emergency treatment in this situation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because emergency treatment should not be withheld pending a Gillick competence assessment.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because court authorisation is not needed before urgent life-saving treatment in an emergency.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
